arabic text: UTHKAY KAFAN CHO WAIKHO, HAYE UTHKAY KAFAN\nCHO WAIKHO\nSADA HAAL RAZA MOLA, LAJPAAL RAZA MOLA
english translation text: Rise from your shroud and look—alas, rise from\nyour shroud and see our condition, O Raza,\nprotector of the forsaken; O compassionate Raza.

arabic text:
EDHI CHAITI KAANU PAIYAN, MOLA RAZA JUDAIYAN
LUTIYAAN NAY BADSHAIYAN,HOGAIYAN NAY TABAIYAN
BAGHDAD DAY QAIDI DA, HAYE BAGHDAD DAY QAIDI
DA
HAYE LAAL RAZA MOLA, LAJPAAL RAZA MOLA
english translation text:
Why did separation come so soon, O Maula Raza?
Kingship has been plundered and everything lies
ruined. The son of Baghdad’s prisoner—alas, the
son of Baghdad’s prisoner— is stricken, O Raza,
protector of the forsaken; O compassionate Raza.

arabic text:
SYED NU ZEHR MILEYA, DIL QAIDIYAN DA HALEYA
BA BERIYAN JO CHALIYA, MARKAY ZINDAN CHON
WALIYA
ABID TAY MUSA KAZIM, HAYE ABID TAY MUSA KAZIM
BAY HAAL RAZA MOLA, LAJPAAL RAZA MOLA
english translation text:
The Sayyid was given poison, and the prisoners’
hearts trembled. The one who had walked in chains
returned from prison only after death. Abid and Musa
al-Kazim—alas, Abid and Musa al-Kazim— are desolate, O
Raza, protector of the forsaken; O compassionate Raza.

arabic text:
CHAIYAN MOUT DIYAN CHAAWAN, BHENA WEKHDIYAN
RAAWAN
AJ RON LAIY BULAWAAN, KARBAL GAIYAN JO MAAWAN
BHAINA DA VICHORA EH, HAYE BHAINA DA VICHORA
EH
TEREY NAAL RAZA MOLA, LAJPAAL RAZA MOLA
english translation text:
The shadows of death have fallen; the
sisters watch the roads. Today let me call
those mothers who went to Karbala to weep. The
sorrow of separation from sisters—alas,
separation from sisters— remains with you, O
Raza, protector of the forsaken; O compassionate Raza.

arabic text:
SYED DI QURBAANI,HAY KHOON DI RAWANI
KARBAL WALI DI RAANI, KHA MOUT GAIY JAWAANI
DUNIYA TON TURR PAIYA EH, HAYE DUNIYA TON TURR
PAIYA EH BAY MISAAL RAZA MOLA, LAJPAAL RAZA MOLA
english translation text:
The Sayyid’s sacrifice, the flowing of blood—
the queen descended from Karbala’s master died in her youth.
She has departed from this world—alas, she has departed from this world—
O peerless Raza, protector of the forsaken; O compassionate Raza.
